articles.title: Supermicro promised a new CFO in December 2024. A $2.5 billion smuggling case and a cofounder’s arrest later, it has one
articles.summary: Tech investor Mark Long has replaced former CFO David Weigand.
articles.body:
Super Micro Computer , the troubled hardware ally of Nvidia and Elon Musk's SpaceX, has finally hired a new head of finance. The appointment comes nearly two years after a board-level independent investigation led the company to commit to "immediately" begin searching for a replacement for longtime chief financial officer David Weigand.

Mark Long, 59, replaced Weigand as CFO on Wednesday—"effective immediately," according to Supermicro—and he brings with him a stack of bona fides. He previously served as CFO and chief strategy officer at $130 billion data storage company Western Digital , and he runs an investment and advisory firm, Prime Impact Capital. Long also served a stint as co-CEO and CFO of a SPAC he cofounded that raised $300 million before it merged in 2023 with a Beijing-based auto insurance technology platform , Cheche Technology.

He joins Supermicro at an incredibly complex moment for the hardware maker with deep ties to Nvidia and its CEO, Jensen Huang, and Musk's xAI , which was folded into SpaceX. Long's record as a veteran executive and tech investor is likely intended to help clear the cloud that has hovered over Supermicro for the past two years and to burnish its credibility with skeptical investors.

In March, the Department of Justice and FBI indicted and arrested Supermicro cofounder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw in a shocking smuggling case allegedly involving $2.5 billion of Supermicro hardware loaded with Nvidia's export-controlled chips being illegally routed to China. Liaw, along with two others associated with Supermicro, was alleged to have gone to extreme lengths to deceive officials, including using hair dryers to remove and replace sticky labels and staging thousands of dummy servers that were nonworking physical replicas of actual Supermicro servers—because the real servers had already been diverted to China.

Supermicro is not named as a defendant in the case, and has said it is cooperating with law enforcement. Liaw has pleaded not guilty. His March arrest, however, kicked off another board-led internal investigation—separate from the previous probe that led to the CFO search—that Supermicro said in August found no evidence that current members of senior management knew about the smuggling scheme.

Until he resigned after being arrested and charged in the smuggling case, Liaw had served on the Supermicro board and had a long history with fellow cofounders Charles Liang and Sara Liu. (Liu and Liang are married and both serve on the Supermicro board.) Liaw had previously left Supermicro in the midst of an internal audit committee investigation just before a 2018 SEC probe charged Supermicro and its then-CFO with improper revenue recognition practices. Supermicro settled the SEC's charges and paid a $17.5 million settlement in 2020. Liaw returned to Supermicro as a consultant in May 2021 and eventually became a full-time employee before rejoining the board in December 2023.

articles.title: Petróleo dispara e Brent chega a US$ 110 pela 1ª vez desde maio; veja o que pressiona os preços | G1
articles.standfirst: Escalada das tensões no Oriente Médio, ataques a instalações de petróleo na Rússia e incertezas sobre a oferta de diesel aumentam a pressão sobre o mercado global de combustíveis.
articles.summary: Escalada das tensões no Oriente Médio, ataques a instalações de petróleo na Rússia e incertezas sobre a oferta de diesel aumentam a pressão sobre o mercado global de combustíveis.
articles.body:
O petróleo Brent atingiu US$ 110 por barril pela primeira vez desde maio , diante do temor de que o aumento das tensões no Oriente Médio restrinja ainda mais a oferta global.

Os contratos futuros do Brent, referência internacional para os preços do petróleo, fecharam nesta sexta-feira (16) em alta de US$ 3,94, ou 3,7%, a US$ 109,86 por barril, o maior valor desde 19 de maio.

Já os contratos do West Texas Intermediate (WTI), referência nos Estados Unidos, subiram US$ 3,44, ou 3,5%, e encerraram o dia a US$ 101,41 por barril, no maior patamar desde 17 de setembro .

Na semana, até o momento, o Brent acumula alta de 4,9% , enquanto o WTI avançou 10,4% .

Segundo a consultoria Energy Aspects, consultada pela Reuters, os preços voltaram a subir após uma queda anterior, em meio ao temor de uma escalada do conflito e a relatos de possíveis ataques à infraestrutura de energia da Arábia Saudita.

Relatos da imprensa israelense indicaram que o Irã poderia estar preparando um ataque preventivo , após serviços de inteligência ocidentais identificarem movimentações militares incomuns.

Embora não tenham sido confirmadas, essas informações reforçaram a preocupação com novos confrontos e possíveis interrupções no fornecimento de petróleo, segundo a consultoria.

Uma coalizão liderada pela Arábia Saudita informou ter interceptado e destruído um míssil balístico lançado em direção a Yanbu , cidade portuária no Mar Vermelho.

🔎 O porto é estratégico para o país porque permite escoar petróleo para o mercado internacional por uma rota alternativa ao Estreito de Ormuz, passagem marítima importante para o transporte global da commodity.

De acordo com a consultoria Rapidan Energy Group, também ouvida pela Reuters, as primeiras informações indicavam que não houve danos à infraestrutura de Yanbu.

A oferta de combustíveis também é motivo de preocupação por causa dos ataques ucranianos a instalações de petróleo russas .

Na quinta-feira (15), a Ucrânia atacou uma refinaria na Rússia, depois que o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, anunciou que Kiev abandonaria a trégua que abrangia instalações de energia.

O cessar-fogo havia sido anunciado pelo presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. Zelenskiy também criticou a disposição de Trump de negociar acordos com Moscou.

A refinaria de Ryazan, na Rússia, interrompeu as operações em uma unidade de destilação primária de petróleo após um ataque com drones na região, na quinta-feira, segundo duas fontes do setor ouvidas pela Reuters.

A destilação primária é uma etapa inicial do refino em que o petróleo é aquecido e separado em diferentes componentes, que podem ser usados na produção de combustíveis , como diesel e gasolina .

Para Dennis Kissler, vice-presidente sênior de operações da BOK Financial, entrevistado pela Reuters, a combinação das tensões no Oriente Médio com as dúvidas sobre a capacidade russa de fornecer diesel tem incentivado os investidores a comprar petróleo.

Na tentativa de ampliar a oferta, a Agência Internacional de Energia (AIE) concordou, na quinta-feira, em liberar mais de 20 milhões de barris de combustíveis no mercado.

Os Estados Unidos também abriram, na sexta-feira (16), uma chamada para propostas de troca de até 17 milhões de barris de petróleo da Reserva Estratégica de Petróleo do país, segundo o Departamento de Energia americano.

A reserva é um estoque mantido pelo governo para ajudar a enfrentar situações de interrupção no abastecimento.

articles.title: Déficit das contas públicas dos EUA sobe a US$ 1,99 trilhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Resultado piorou em US$ 217 bilhões em um ano fiscal, com gastos recordes e alta nas despesas com a dívida pública; reembolsos de tarifas derrubadas pela Justiça americana também pressionaram as contas.
articles.summary: Resultado piorou em US$ 217 bilhões em um ano fiscal, com gastos recordes e alta nas despesas com a dívida pública; reembolsos de tarifas derrubadas pela Justiça americana também pressionaram as contas.
articles.body:
O déficit das contas públicas dos Estados Unidos subiu para US$ 1,99 trilhão no ano fiscal de 2026, encerrado em 30 de setembro, alta de US$ 217 bilhões em relação ao período anterior.

O resultado é o maior em cinco anos e foi impulsionado por gastos recordes do governo, pelo aumento das despesas com a dívida pública e por reembolsos de tarifas de importação, segundo dados divulgados nesta sexta-feira (16) pelo Departamento do Tesouro americano.

O resultado representa o primeiro ano fiscal completo do segundo mandato do presidente Donald Trump. Em 2025, o déficit havia sido de US$ 1,78 trilhão.

Apesar do aumento, o resultado ficou abaixo do registrado em 2021, quando o déficit chegou a US$ 2,77 trilhões, em meio aos gastos do governo para enfrentar os efeitos da pandemia de Covid-19. O resultado de 2026 é o terceiro maior déficit anual já registrado pelos Estados Unidos.

🔍 Déficit público ocorre quando o governo gasta mais do que arrecada em impostos e outras receitas. Para cobrir essa diferença, o governo precisa buscar recursos, geralmente por meio da emissão de títulos da dívida pública.

As despesas do governo americano somaram US$ 7,40 trilhões no ano fiscal de 2026, um recorde e um aumento de 6% em relação aos US$ 7,01 trilhões registrados no período anterior.

As receitas também atingiram um patamar recorde, de US$ 5,40 trilhões, alta de 3% na comparação com os US$ 5,24 trilhões de 2025.

Mesmo com o aumento da arrecadação, as despesas cresceram em ritmo mais acelerado, ampliando o déficit das contas públicas.

Uma das principais pressões sobre o orçamento foi o custo do serviço da dívida pública . Os gastos com juros e outras despesas relacionadas ao endividamento somaram US$ 1,36 trilhão, alta de US$ 144 bilhões, ou 12%, em relação ao ano anterior.

Com esse resultado, o serviço da dívida se tornou a terceira maior categoria de gastos do governo americano, atrás apenas da Previdência Social e das despesas combinadas com os programas Medicare e Medicaid, que financiam serviços de saúde.

A dívida pública total dos Estados Unidos ultrapassou US$ 40 trilhões cerca de dois meses antes da divulgação dos dados.

Reembolsos de tarifas pressionam as contas

Outro fator que contribuiu para o aumento do déficit foi a redução da receita líquida com tarifas de importação.

Após uma decisão da Suprema Corte americana que derrubou grande parte das tarifas impostas por Trump em seu primeiro ano de mandato, o governo teve de realizar reembolsos a importadores.

Segundo a Reuters, os reembolsos somaram US$ 145 bilhões no ano fiscal de 2026. Com isso, a receita líquida com tarifas caiu US$ 22 bilhões, uma redução de 11%, para cerca de US$ 173 bilhões.

O Tesouro americano estimou que o déficit correspondeu a 6,2% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) em 2026, acima da proporção de 5,8% registrada no ano fiscal de 2025.

Em setembro, último mês do ano fiscal, o governo registrou déficit de US$ 27 bilhões. No mesmo mês do ano anterior, havia sido registrado superávit de US$ 198 bilhões.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com membros da imprensa após desembarcar do Air Force One, depois de participar de um comício de campanha em Clarksville, Tennessee, na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, Maryland, EUA, em 10 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Eric Lee

articles.title: Tarifa zero nos ônibus pode reduzir inflação em 0,25 ponto, mas arrecadação atual já não cobre custos, diz ANTP | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta anunciada por Lula prevê gratuidade no transporte coletivo urbano aos sábados, domingos e feriados a partir de 2027, caso seja reeleito; estimativa aponta queda de 22,4% no preço do subitem ônibus urbano do IPCA.
articles.summary: Proposta anunciada por Lula prevê gratuidade no transporte coletivo urbano aos sábados, domingos e feriados a partir de 2027, caso seja reeleito.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, candidato à reeleição, anunciou nesta quinta-feira (15) que enviará ao Congresso Nacional uma Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) para garantir transporte coletivo urbano gratuito aos finais de semana e feriados .

A estimativa é que a medida reduza em 0,25 ponto percentual o Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA) no mês em que a PEC for aprovada, explica Leonardo Costa, economista do ASA, instituição financeira.

A medida passaria a valer em 2027 , caso Lula vença a eleição deste mês.

Veja o post de Lula no X, antigo Twitter:

O cálculo de redução da inflação considera uma queda de aproximadamente 22,4% no preço do subitem ônibus urbano, que representa 1,116% do índice. A estimativa já leva em conta as cidades que oferecem gratuidade atualmente e aquelas em que a cobrança ainda existe.

Para a Associação Nacional dos Transportes Públicos (ANTP), "hoje a receita proveniente do pagamento da tarifa pública não é suficiente para cobrir os custos operacionais do sistema de transporte, o que requer o aporte de receitas não tarifárias".

Tal aporte já vem sendo feito pelo país por meio de subsídios públicos, "embora insuficientes para mudar a sua qualidade no Brasil", complementa. "São necessárias outras fontes de recursos para o que o sistema seja sustentado, com melhoria".

"Ao mesmo tempo em que a tarifa zero representa o atendimento a um direito social constitucioal, são necessárias fontes seguras de recursos para suportar de forma perene a qualidade e todos os custos operacionais, o que não vem ocorrendo", escreve a ANTP em nota.

No entanto, a ANTP entende que o processo de implantação de tarifa zero deve ser progressiva, incorporando a gratuidade inicialmente para a população mais pobre, e que a tarifa pública seja baixa, ao alcance das demais faixas de renda da população.

"É imperativa a participação do Governo Federal no custeio da operação do transporte público", enfatiza.

Cidades já adotam gratuidade ou desconto

"A medida se soma às experiências já em curso em algumas capitais, que mostram como a gratuidade aos domingos pode funcionar na prática", afirma Costa.

Em São Paulo , o programa Domingão Tarifa Zero começou em dezembro de 2023 e oferece gratuidade nos ônibus municipais aos domingos.

Em Belo Horizonte , a gratuidade entrou em vigor em 14 de dezembro de 2025, por decreto, como parte do programa Catraca Livre . A medida abrange todas as linhas convencionais e suplementares aos domingos e feriados nacionais.

Em Belém , os ônibus das empresas associadas ao Sindicato das Empresas de Transporte de Passageiros de Belém (Setransbel) passaram a ser gratuitos aos domingos e feriados em 13 de abril de 2025.

Brasília também adotou a gratuidade nesses dias, no início de fevereiro de 2025.

Curitiba , por sua vez, optou por um desconto em vez da isenção total. Desde 5 de janeiro de 2025, a tarifa aos domingos e feriados custa R$ 3, o equivalente a um desconto de 50% sobre o valor regular.

articles.title: The US economy is facing 2 hot wars heating up at a bad time for the White House
articles.summary: The wars in Iran and Ukraine are heating up at a bad moment for the US economy and the White House.
articles.body:
Yields are above multidecade highs , both gas and diesel prices continue to climb , and critical midterm elections are around the corner.

Adding to pressure on the US economy and the current administration, the world's two largest hot wars are heating up.

In the Middle East, dual fronts along the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea have seen a resurgence of conflict in recent weeks that has heavily disrupted oil flows in the region.

Multiple tankers and container ships in the Strait of Hormuz either caught fire or sank this week in the Iran-dominated waterway. The Washington Institute has tracked more than two dozen attacks recorded since the start of the month.

President Trump has said the US military won't resume airstrikes inside Iran before the midterm elections as White House negotiators continue angling for a diplomatic solution to the conflict now in its eighth month.

At the same time, administration officials are reportedly war-gaming a major offensive to come after the November elections, when the president will be less encumbered by the political needs of the Republican Party.

"The Trump Administration does not want Brent crude oil at $106/bbl going into the midterm elections, just a month away, and has said that he only plans to escalate offenses against Iran after the midterms are over, with what he hopes to be, a red wave," Rabobank cross-asset macro strategist Molly Schwartz said in a recent note to clients.

To the west along the Red Sea, Yemen's Houthi militants have sharply escalated their campaign against the Saudi coalition opposing the group's bid for wider territorial control, launching multiple rounds of strikes on major airports inside the kingdom that have killed more than a dozen people and wounded hundreds.

Houthi militants recently struck an office building belonging to the state-managed oil giant Saudi Aramco ( 2223.SR ). While the kingdom's oil production remains largely undisrupted, violent pestering by the Iran-allied Houthis is driving up oil prices .

"Iran knows when the midterms are too," Schwartz added, "and if they want to further complicate Trump's plans, now is the perfect time to have the Houthis stir up trouble and make it increasingly difficult for the US to avoid intervening."

Ukraine, Russia, and Starlink throttling

Ukraine and Russia, which have been at war since Russia executed a stealth annexation of Crimea in 2014 and invaded its neighbor in February 2022, recently both escalated offensive strikes against critical infrastructure ahead of another winter.

articles.title: Goldman flags 2 memory stocks to buy amid deeper sector pullback
articles.summary: Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs told clients in a new note that two names offer an attractive risk/reward after a sharp sell-off in memory stocks.
articles.body:
Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs told clients in a new note that two names offer an attractive risk/reward after a sharp sell-off in memory stocks.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are the stocks in question. The bank argued that the market has overestimated China's ability to close the technology gap.

Shares of major memory suppliers, including Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, SanDisk, Kioxia and CXMT, have fallen 11% to 26% since Oct. 10. The decline has wiped well over $700 billion from the sector's market value.

The slide followed news that Chinese DRAM maker CXMT had made progress on a new "4F2" cell architecture. Its president also said the company plans to roll out a server-memory product based on the technology by the end of 2026.

Goldman said other factors likely contributed to the drop, including credit and AI financing concerns and a higher-than-expected CPI reading.

It noted that CXMT's own shares fell, as did NAND suppliers that are less exposed to the technology. DRAM spot prices, meanwhile, have continued to trend higher.

"Bottom line, while we believe some concerns on the technology progress are appropriate and the capacity gap is narrowing, we believe there is still a significant technology gap, especially in advanced node DRAM and HBM," the analysts wrote.

Goldman feels the market has underestimated China's capacity ramp-up but overestimated the potential for a technology breakthrough. It pointed to the time needed to complete customer qualifications, reach high-yield mass production and narrow the gap in HBM.

Samsung trades at 1.2 times price-to-book on 2027 estimates and 0.9 times on 2028 estimates, while Hynix trades at 1.4 times and 0.9 times. Goldman said these below-book valuations imply that a downcycle is priced in by 2028, "which is much more pessimistic compared to our 'higher for longer' view."

The bank cautioned that there may be few catalysts for a quick recovery in the share prices in the near term.

articles.summary: When the US-Iran war began at the end of February, it unleashed an energy crisis on the world and one not seen in recent years.
articles.body: When the US-Iran war began at the end of February, it unleashed an energy crisis on the world and one not seen in recent years. Oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, de facto controlled by Iran, came to a standstill, crude oil prices shot up, and the world was left grappling with a supply crunch.The US war with Iran exposed Tehran’s ability to disrupt the global economy by blocking the Strait of Hormuz. Before the war, around 19 million barrels of crude oil were exported daily from the Middle East.However, September data from tanker-tracking firm Kpler showed oil flows recovering to an average of 16 million barrels per day, the highest since the conflict began.Of this, around 10 million barrels passed through the Strait of Hormuz, while another 6 million barrels moved through pipelines and ports on the Red Sea and Gulf of Oman that bypass the strait.But a deal between the US and Iran is still elusive. Does that mean that Iran has lost the hold it had over the Strait of Hormuz? How sustainable are the oil flows through Hormuz and what does the increased supply mean for India? And importantly, if supply is normalizing, then why are prices of oil not coming down?Hormuz grip: Is Iran losing leverage?Export volumes exceeded pre-war levels on 14 days during September. The figures covered oil shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, supplies routed via the Red Sea, as well as crude loaded at terminals and transferred between vessels in the Gulf of Oman.Kpler data shows more oil flowing through Hormuz against the spring and summer trough. But, it also suggests that flows are slipping again in October.Gulf crude exports recovered to 14.1 mb/d in September from 9.8 mb/d in August (+4.3 mb/d m/m), about 78% of February’s 18.2 mb/d, though this includes bypass loadings at Yanbu and Fujairah, according to Naveen Das, Senior Analyst at Kpler.“Kpler’s crossing data show crude through the strait down 27% from a wartime high to at least 10.1 mb/d, and my tally of Strait of Hormuz feed shows laden exits falling from about 11.0 mb/d (1-7 Oct) to 6.2 mb/d (8-12 Oct),” Naveen Das tells TOI.But, in an analysis, Kpler has actually said that normalisation of flows via Hormuz no longer needs a deal. Kpler’s base case instead reflects slower, uneven normalisation under continued conflict, with shipping recovering through operational adaptation rather than following a single diplomatic trigger. “Washington appears willing to sustain economic pressure while facilitating shipping,” Kpler has said in a recent report.According to an NYT article, the recovery in oil flows suggests the US has reduced Iran’s control over the waterway, but it has come at a high cost.Costs are several times higher: VLCCs loading at Fujairah, Yanbu or Muscat are fixing at 750-950 WS against 125-155 quoted for Gulf loadings in February. War-risk premiums are quoted at 3-8% of hull value, against about 0.25% pre-war.Also, Iran continues to attack ships almost daily, yet more tankers are now willing to risk the crossing. The US military has been providing air protection, while Saudi Arabia and the UAE have increased payments to tanker operators, with fees in some cases reaching ten times pre-war levels, the NYT report said.Iran is under growing economic pressure, with years of sanctions compounded by the war. Its own seaborne oil exports have fallen to zero under the US blockade, according to Kpler.However, as per NYT analysis Iran’s broader strategy of keeping oil prices high enough to pressure the US and the global economy remains effective.Iran also retains other options if it comes under greater pressure. Its allies, the Houthis in Yemen, control the Bab al-Mandab Strait, another important shipping route. Tehran could also target Gulf energy infrastructure.What needs to be understood is that even though Iran’s grip on Hormuz may be weakening as oil shipments resume, its ability to keep energy costs high and threaten other critical routes means its leverage over the US has not disappeared.And the threat is not yet over.According to Kpler data, last week saw the most tanker attacks of any week of the war, and only seven commodity vessels crossed on October 6th, the fewest since July 23, against about 125 a day pre-war. At least six vessels have been hit since September 28, and Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline was shut after the 10-11 September attacks and is only about half restored.Why are crude oil prices not coming down?Despite the increase in oil flows, prices have not fallen significantly. Higher tanker fees and insurance premiums continue to make shipments expensive, while global supplies remain insufficient to meet demand. China and other countries are also drawing down the reserves that helped cushion the initial disruption, and approaching winter is expected to increase demand for heating fuel.Several factors are contributing to the persistently high crude oil prices, the biggest among them being the uncertainty surrounding the transit of oil and the future of war.“A combination of unsustainable flows, the threat of attacks and the need to access crude oil promptly before high freight rates dent refinery margins are keeping prices elevated for now. All of these factors are difficult to resolve, which is why the baseline oil price is remaining elevated,” explains Naveen Das.The market is not going by the increase in the number of barrels that are loaded and transiting. It is pricing in the risks related to the reliability and usability of supply.While recovering exports may have eased the physical shortage, they have not removed the underlying delivery risk, high freight costs, refinery constraints or even the depleted inventories.Praveen Rai, Director, Grant Thornton Bharat lists four key reasons for oil prices remaining high:First, the risk of renewed interruption remains embedded in prices. A cargo loaded today does not guarantee that the next shipment will move safely or arrive on schedule.Second, logistics remain exceptionally expensive. Industry shipping estimates indicate that Middle East-to-Asia very large crude carrier rates recently exceeded $1.2 million per day, compared with roughly $30,000 in January, and that freight represented about 27% of the delivered value of a barrel on the observed route, compared with about 3% previously.Third, the constraint extends beyond crude availability. The International Energy Agency reports that global diesel exports in September were approximately 700,000 barrels per day below the previous year, as a 1.3 million barrel-per-day loss from Russia and the Middle East was only partly offset by other suppliers. Global observed oil inventories were also 509 million barrels below end-February levels. This means the market has fewer product and inventory buffers even as crude loadings recover.Finally, crude quality and refinery availability matter. More crude exports do not automatically translate into more diesel, particularly when medium-sour grades and refinery capacity are constrained.“Durable price relief will require safer passage, lower freight and insurance costs, improved refinery operations and a recovery in inventories, alongside higher supply,” Rai says.What it means for IndiaBefore the start of the conflict, oil from the Middle East made up a big part of India’s crude imports. In fact, not just crude, India’s dependency on the Middle East for LPG and LNG imports was also high.So, easing of supplies through the Hormuz carries significant implications for India, especially at a time when alternative barrels from Russia become more expensive in the face of competition for oil procurement from China.According to Naveen Das, India has kept total imports at about 5.0-5.3 million barrels per day and swapped origins, buying wherever risk-adjusted landed cost is lowest.“Russia rose from 1.08 mb/d in February to a 2.73 mb/d peak in July, then eased to 1.87 mb/d in September (-12% m/m). The Gulf-origin share fell from about 59% in February to about 18% in June and is back to about 37% in September,” he notes.“Iraq plus Kuwait rose from 0.32 mb/d in August to 0.86 mb/d in September, so India is again exposed to inside-strait barrels, not just bypass volumes. Venezuela is a new 0.2-0.35 mb/d supplier since April,” he adds.Praveen Rai believes that the improved Gulf availability has given Indian refiners greater access to medium-sour grades suited to producing diesel and other middle distillates.“Supplier-arranged shuttle and ship-to-ship transfers can reduce a buyer’s direct exposure to the highest-risk leg, but the allocation of freight, insurance and transit risk depends on the commercial terms of each cargo,” he says.India’s strategy remains optionality: a wider pool of available suppliers improves substitution and refinery planning.“The limitation is that supplier diversification is not necessarily route diversification, since several Gulf suppliers remain exposed to the same chokepoint. However, India remains committed to securing for itself the best mix of crude considering various geopolitical factors and market and national imperatives,” Rai tells TOI.So while India is managing to procure crude via its diversified crude basket, the risk of flows via Hormuz continues, and whatever is coming is being bought at high rates, which ultimately continues to exert pressure on inflation and the economy.You use AI every day. articles.title: CoreWeave stock sinks as AI financing worries linger
articles.summary: CoreWeave stock  got clobbered again on Friday as fears over AI financing lingered
articles.body:
CoreWeave ( CRWV ) stock as much as 10% on Friday as concerns over AI funding continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

The decline comes after CoreWeave stock rebounded from a 7% drop on Thursday, following comments from ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang that helped ease concerns over the company's debt-heavy balance sheet.

"CoreWeave's strength is improving every day," Huang shared at a Bloomberg event in Stockholm. "I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing."

A viral chart showing CoreWeave's spiking bond yields earlier this week underscored concerns about the company's debt-heavy balance sheet and whether it can scale its business quickly enough to cover rising interest expenses.

Nvidia's backing is significant , given that the AI chip giant holds roughly 47.2 million shares of CoreWeave, representing about a 10% stake in the company.

CoreWeave is also a major customer of Nvidia's chips, underscoring the close ties between the two companies.

CoreWeave was on track to finish the week down 21% as of Thursday's close, following a volatile stretch.

Meanwhile, peer Nebius ( NBIS ) fell 5% in early trading, putting it on course for weekly losses as well.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: LTM Q2 revenue grows 4.7% to $1.2 bn in Q2; AI biz revenue up 47%
articles.summary: LTM Q2 revenue rose 4.7% YoY to $1.2B; AI business up 47%. EBIT margin 15.6%, order inflow $1.2B, interim dividend Rs 25/share.
articles.body: Bengaluru: LTM’s dollar revenue rose 1% sequentially and 4.7% year-on-year to $1.2 billion in the September quarter. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 1.1% quarter-on-quarter and 5.1% year-on-year.EBIT margin stood at 15.6%, up 10 basis points from the previous quarter but down 30 basis points year-on-year. The margin has recovered from a low of 15.1% in the March quarter but remains below the 16.1% recorded in the December quarter.LTM’s headcount rose to 88,835, with 949 employees added during the quarter and 2,388 over the year. Trailing 12-month attrition was 13.3%, down 90 basis points year-on-year. Utilisation, excluding trainees, remained at 86.4%, 170 basis points below the year-ago level.CEO and managing director Venu Lambu attributed the performance to the company’s AI strategy. “Our broad-based performance reflects the successful execution of our AI-centric strategy. The revenue across Enterprise AI and Business AI together grew 47% YoY,” he said.Lambu said the strategy had also helped LTM add a financial services client to its $100 million-plus revenue category. The company was “well positioned for stronger growth ahead”, he said.Order inflow stood at $1.2 billion, down from $1.6 billion in Q1 FY27. Active clients declined to 729 from 740 in the previous quarter, despite the addition of 20 new clients. However, the number of clients in the $100 million-plus revenue category rose to three, while the $10 million-plus category reached 109.The board approved an interim dividend of Rs 25 per equity share.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ather gets insurance nod, eyes income beyond scooter sales
articles.summary: Ather Energy gets Irdai approval for Ather Insurance as a composite corporate agent, enabling distribution of life, general and health policies to add recurring revenue.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Electric scooter maker Ather Energy is expanding its footprint into insurance distribution, seeking to earn recurring income from its customers through a subsidiary that has secured regulatory approval.Insurance regulator Irdai granted Ather Insurance, its wholly owned subsidiary, registration as a composite corporate agent on October 15. This allows the company to distribute and service life, general and health insurance policies, Ather said in a stock exchange disclosure.The licence permits Ather Insurance to act as an intermediary selling policies issued by insurers. It does not authorise the subsidiary to underwrite insurance or take on the risks covered by those policies.Ather said the business would help broaden its sources of revenue by tapping its existing customer base. It also expects the move to improve the experience of customers and retail partners. The disclosure did not name insurance partners, give a launch timeline or estimate the income the business could generate.The registration took effect on October 15 and will continue subject to payment of an annual fee, unless suspended or cancelled by Irdai.Insurance will add to Ather’s businesses beyond vehicle sales. Software subscriptions, charging, accessories, spares and servicing together contributed 13% of its total income in FY26. The company reported total income of Rs 3,823 crore for the year, up 66%.Ather remained loss-making, although its annual net loss narrowed to Rs 517.2 crore from Rs 812.3 crore in FY25.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Ready to work with India’: China says it does not seek trade surplus as Sitharaman flags market access barriers
articles.summary: China on Friday said it was ready to work with India to address their respective economic and trade concerns after finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
articles.body: China on Friday said it was ready to work with India to address their respective economic and trade concerns after finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman criticised Beijing's restrictions on market access for Indian products, citing them as a major factor behind the widening trade deficit.“What I can tell you is that China never aims for trade surplus,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said during a media briefing, responding to a question on Sitharaman's remarks.“We stand ready to work with India to address each other’s economic and trade concerns in a balanced way and promote the steady development of bilateral relations,” Mao said, adding that questions on the issue should be directed to the relevant Chinese authorities.The response came after Sitharaman said that India's growing trade imbalance with China and persistent restrictions on market access for Indian goods remained major concerns despite years of engagement between the two countries.India flags non-tariff barriersSpeaking at an interactive session with the Atlantic Council on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, Sitharaman said non-tariff barriers remained the biggest obstacle to trade between India and China.“Non-tariff barriers are the biggest hurdle in the trade between India and China,” she said, adding that India had repeatedly raised concerns over the lack of market access for its products.Sitharaman said Indian goods faced persistent restrictions in China despite significant opportunities in sectors where India was globally competitive. These included generic medicines, bovine meat, vegetables and other perishable products.She said India had spent nearly a decade seeking better access for its products in the Chinese market, but had made little progress.The finance minister also criticised China's use of phytosanitary measures and other non-tariff restrictions, arguing that such issues could be resolved through investigations and discussions between the two countries.Sitharaman said India had not adopted the approach of imposing punitive tariffs or countervailing duties to correct trade imbalances, preferring to pursue negotiations despite the time and effort involved.She added that the trade imbalance with China had continued to grow over several years, making it difficult for India to address the disparity through dialogue alone.India-China trade deficit widens to $105.93 billionThe remarks came after data released by China Customs on Wednesday showed that India's trade deficit with China widened to $105.93 billion during January-September, a 20.7 per cent increase from the corresponding period last year.Bilateral trade during the nine-month period rose 25.4 per cent to $144.45 billion, according to the data.China's exports to India increased 23.3 per cent to $125.19 billion, while India's exports to China rose 40.7 per cent to $19.26 billion.Despite the faster growth in Indian exports, the substantially higher value of imports from China kept the trade balance heavily tilted in Beijing's favour.India has consistently sought greater access to the Chinese market for products in sectors such as information technology, pharmaceuticals and agricultural goods.However, Sitharaman said persistent non-tariff barriers had continued to limit opportunities for Indian exporters.Both sides signal willingness to improve trade tiesThe latest exchange comes as New Delhi has indicated efforts to rebuild its economic relationship with Beijing.Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said earlier this week that India was working to rebuild ties with China, adding that the outcome of the process remained uncertain.Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal also said the two countries were holding discussions on trade-related issues.“There are discussions going on on both sides on trade issues also...constant discussions will help improve the trade ties between the two countries,” Agrawal said, according to news agency PTI.While China has now expressed its willingness to address trade concerns in a balanced manner, India continues to highlight market access restrictions and the widening deficit as key issues in its economic engagement with Beijing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Middle east war hits Indian fuel retailers: OMCs losing up to Rs 30 per litre on sales, says report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Selling petrol and diesel has become increasingly costly for India's oil marketing companies (OMCs).
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Selling petrol and diesel has become increasingly costly for India's oil marketing companies (OMCs). A Jefferies report estimated that they are losing Rs 26 on every litre of petrol and Rs 30 on diesel as the Middle East conflict drives up crude procurement and shipping costs.The estimates, based on 15-day average prices, point to a widening gap between what fuel retailers spend on procuring crude and what they recover through domestic fuel sales.In its report, "Energy Market Letter: Volume XXII", Jefferies said the cost of procuring crude for Indian OMCs was comparable to an Indian crude basket price of $125 per barrel."Marketing margins deep in the red: Procurement cost for OMCs is similar to the Indian crude basket price of US$ 125/bbl, leading to steep losses," the report stated, as cited by ANI.A major factor behind the squeeze is the surge in freight costs, which have risen eightfold since the conflict began. Shipping now makes up more than a quarter of the landed cost of crude oil, against just 3 per cent before the war.Jefferies said freight rates had climbed another 8 per cent over the past week, adding to the cost of bringing oil into India.The pressure has been compounded by a fresh disruption to crude shipments from the Middle East. Excluding Iran, oil flows from the region have fallen to around 75 per cent of pre-war levels, compared with approximately 95 per cent at the end of September."Overall flows (ex-Iran) have declined to ~75% of pre-war level (~95% at end-Sep) due to heightened attacks in the Gulf of Oman," Jefferies said.The figures suggest that the recovery in regional oil shipments seen towards the end of September has reversed, leaving import-dependent countries such as India exposed to higher supply and transportation costs.While Jefferies noted that refining margins remain elevated, the benefit is being offset on the fuel marketing side by the higher cost of crude procurement.For Indian OMCs, the immediate challenge is therefore not just the price of crude oil, but also the sharply higher cost of transporting it. Continued disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies could keep marketing margins under pressure even if refining operations remain profitable.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: From e-cigarettes to abortion rights: A look at how big banks made debanking calls
articles.summary: Regulators reviewed roughly 50,000 documents from nine large US banks and found that lenders sometimes relied on reputational concerns rather than outright f...
articles.body:
A merchant selling MAGA gear, a religious nonprofit with public views on same-sex marriage, and an abortion rights group whose political donations went overwhelmingly to Democrats.

These were some of the current and prospective customers that the nation's largest banks denied services to, according to a report released this week that offers more details on how political and religious views influenced banks' risk assessments behind closed doors.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), which reviewed roughly 50,000 documents from nine large US banks, found that lenders sometimes relied on reputational concerns rather than outright financial risks when deciding whom to bank. Regulators said a range of industries were targeted, including oil and gas exploration, coal mining, firearms manufacturing, detention facilities, and tobacco and e-cigarette retailers.

The report shed further light on how those decisions played out, including disrupting a religious nonprofit's fundraising process and eliminating a merchant's access to payment services.

The OCC stopped short of determining that the individual cases violated federal law. Federal protections against political discrimination in banking vary.

In the months following the Jan. 6 Capitol riots in 2021, a payments processor owned by JPMorgan Chase closed the accounts of two different merchants selling Donald Trump and MAGA gear after concluding that the products promoted hate, violence, or racial intolerance.

Months later, it did the same to another payments processor after the event organizer "called President Biden and Dr. Anthony Fauci 'the enemy' and characterized Black Lives Matter as Marxists" on social media. Employees for WePay and JPMorgan decided the posts were an "incitement of hate," according to the report.

"[T]here is no set criteria to indicate if A, B, or C word is found to be considered as hate or racism or terrorism, etc," a JPMorgan risk employee later noted. The account closure was ultimately reversed.

A JPMorgan spokesperson said the process used by WePay, a payments technology company it acquired and has since shut down, "did not meet our expectations."

"We identified it, corrected it, and the business no longer operates," the bank said in a statement, adding that its policies prohibit discrimination based on political or religious views and that the report highlighted "a limited number of historical interactions among the nearly 90 million customers and small businesses we serve."

While the OCC's findings offer more examples of conservatives encountering so-called debanking issues, the report also highlights that those difficulties weren't exclusive to right-wingers.

articles.title: 'Something extraordinary': Tesla Roadster wows with compressed air thrusters for limited flight
articles.summary: Tesla finally unveiled the long-awaited Roadster on Thursday night.
articles.body:
After a two-week delay, the Tesla ( TSLA ) Roadster event went off with a massive bang — a flying one.

The wedge-shaped, cyberpunk-looking Roadster EV appeared in front of an inverted half roller coaster ramp erected at SpaceX's facility in Waco, Texas. The Roadster cruised halfway up — glued to the ramp using a vacuum fan system — then launched off the ramp upside down and performed flips in the air, using air thrusters to right itself and land on the tarmac.

Then the Roadster performed a similar stunt, jumping over several Teslas (including a semi), inverted itself, and then used its thrusters to land — an automaker first.

"Well, it worked," CEO Elon Musk deadpanned.

The Roadster also went 0-60 mph in less than 1 second (0.81 seconds) during a test Tesla conducted at the event. While Tesla claimed the car could hit a top speed of 230 mph, Musk boasted that the production version could target half the speed of sound, or Mach 0.5 (383 mph).

So when can you expect to get one? "We enter production in 2028," Musk said.

Tesla said the car comes in three configurations:

Performance: road-ready, seats 2, with multi-mode suction system for next-level performance on and off track;

Thrust: race-ready, seats 2, with multi-mode suction system and rear-mounted cold-gas thrusters that enable 0–60 in <1 second

Rocket: air-ready, seats 1, with multi-mode suction system, plus perimeter-mounted cold-gas thrusters for forward, upward acceleration and lateral rotational movement. So ... yes, it can fly.

Tesla said the three versions had a range exceeding 300 miles, with a top speed of up to 230 mph for the Rocket version. Officially, in terms of performance, 0- 60 mph across the range is <1.6 seconds for Performance, <0.9 seconds for Thrust, and <0.59 seconds for Rocket.

No word yet on how the Rocket version, with its thrusters that allow short flights, would be allowed on public roads.

The event came two weeks after the initial Oct. 1 reveal date. Tesla said the reveal was pushed back due to weather conditions at the demo site, SpaceX's ( SPCX ) Rocket Development and Testing facility in Waco, Texas .

Tesla is asking prospective buyers to put down a $5,000 deposit, followed by a $45,000 wire transfer due within 10 days of the initial deposit for the performance version, and a $250,000 deposit for the thrust variant. The rocket version is invite-only; no MSRP amounts were released.

" There were hints that the Tesla Roadster might do something extraordinary, but I think what happened in Texas on Thursday evening far exceeded everyone's expectations," said Henry Catchpole, host of Hagerty's "The Driver's Seat," who was in attendance at the event. "How it all translates into a finished, usable, enjoyable road car for enthusiasts remains to be seen. For now, it seems like an incredible engineering achievement ."

articles.title: US seeks bids to exchange 17 million barrels of crude from strategic reserve
articles.summary: The United States is preparing to offer up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) as Washington steps up efforts to
articles.body: The United States is preparing to offer up to 17 million barrels of crude oil from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) as Washington steps up efforts to ease pressure on fuel prices amid disruptions caused by the war with Iran.The US Department of Energy on Friday issued a request for proposals for the latest exchange, under which companies would borrow crude from the emergency stockpile and return oil at a later date, reported Reuters.The move forms part of a broader international effort announced in March to stabilise energy markets after the conflict disrupted oil supplies and sent prices higher.At the time, Washington committed to making 172 million barrels available from its strategic reserves as part of a coordinated International Energy Agency (IEA) initiative involving around 30 countries. The wider arrangement aimed to release 400 million barrels of emergency oil stocks worldwide.However, an earlier attempt to offer the remaining barrels under the US commitment met with limited demand from energy companies.In June, companies agreed to borrow only about 500,000 barrels after being required to return additional crude equivalent to premiums of up to 24 per cent, raising questions about the attractiveness of the exchange terms.The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) is the country's emergency stockpile of crude oil, maintained to help cushion supply disruptions and stabilise energy markets during crises. Under an exchange programme, companies can borrow oil from the reserve and return it later, usually with additional barrels as a premium.The latest proposal follows other attempts to increase global fuel supplies. Earlier this month, Trump reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Russian diesel exports, with an initial 300,000 tonnes expected to be released. The move drew criticism from Ukraine and European leaders, who warned that easing restrictions could benefit Moscow financially.Separately, G7 leaders announced on October 2 that they would implement a coordinated release of 100 million barrels of emergency oil stocks through the IEA over four months. The plan included an accelerated release of diesel supplies to address shortages in international markets.Despite these measures, energy markets remain under strain. Brent crude was trading around $106 a barrel on Friday, with continuing attacks on Gulf shipping and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz keeping supply concerns elevated.You use AI every day. articles.title: Palantir's record breakout unravels as software stocks shed $260 billion
articles.summary: Palantir (PLTR) was breaking records earlier this week and is now heading for correction territory.
articles.body:
Palantir ( PLTR ) was breaking records earlier this week. Now its breakout has reversed, with the stock heading toward correction territory.

Shares are falling roughly 7% Friday, erasing about $34 billion in market value.

The closing number to watch is $188.15. Below that, Palantir would finish more than 10% beneath its October 9 record close, confirming a correction, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

It took nearly a year to reclaim the old record. The victory lasted three trading sessions.

Palantir closed above its November 2025 intraday high near $208 last Friday, then reached nearly $213 Monday. By Wednesday, it was back below the old ceiling. Friday's early move above $203 has given way to another retreat.

That's a bull trap — a breakout above resistance that reverses, leaving investors who chased the move nursing losses.

Software's morning rally is suffering a similar fate.

In a Yahoo Finance basket of 45 software stocks, 43 are falling, and 15 are losing at least 5%. Combined market-value losses exceed $260 billion, including roughly $83 billion at Microsoft ( MSFT ).

ServiceNow ( NOW ) went from gaining nearly 4% to losing over 5%. Salesforce ( CRM ) surrendered an advance of over 2% and is trading roughly 3% lower. Twilio ( TWLO ) is falling double digits, heading for its worst day since August 2025.

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF ( IGV ) is losing nearly 5%, putting its worst day since April in play. Its October and year-to-date gains are gone.

The reversal comes just as investors were warming to software again.

As Yahoo Finance's Michael B. Kelley reported Monday , BofA double-upgraded Salesforce to Buy from Underperform, arguing that fears of AI displacing its platforms were overdone.

"If anything, AI should deepen dependence on these platforms," analyst Tal Liani wrote.

Cybersecurity stocks are taking a beating

The First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF ( CIBR ) is down roughly 10% this week, on track for its worst week since March 2020. Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) and CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) are each losing roughly 18% for the week.

Reported OpenAI talks to acquire security firm Trail of Bits have revived competition concerns. Yet Palo Alto and CrowdStrike are also partners in Anthropic's new cybersecurity initiative , showing how AI companies can be collaborators as well as potential competitors.

For Palantir, rapid growth still comes with towering expectations.

In its August earnings report, the company posted 93% second-quarter revenue growth and reported $9.2 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term Treasurys. Even after Friday's selling, its market value is roughly 55 times the annual revenue it projected at the time. That leaves plenty of growth priced in.

articles.title: Cult.fit gets Sebi nod for IPO with Rs 950 cr fresh issue
articles.summary: Cult.fit gets Sebi approval for IPO with Rs 950 crore fresh issue plus offer for sale of 17.8 crore shares; proceeds to repay debt and expand centres.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Fitness platform Cult.fit has received Sebi’s clearance for its IPO, comprising a fresh issue of up to Rs 950 crore and an offer for sale of 17.8 crore shares.Sebi granted clearance on Oct 12, according to its latest update. The company had filed its draft IPO papers on July 7.The company’s statement did not announce the issue dates or price band. The total offer size will depend on the share price. Money raised from the sale of existing shares will go to the selling shareholders.Cult.fit, earlier known as Curefit Healthcare, plans to use the money from the new shares to repay loans and open more Cult Elite and Cult Neo fitness centres. It will also invest in its subsidiary, Cultsport, to open stores selling its branded fitness products.The money will also help pay rent and other lease-related costs at selected existing centres, as well as fund advertising and general business expenses.Cult.fit had 708 fitness centres across 77 cities as of March this year. According to a Redseer report cited by the company, its network was four times the size of the next largest player in India.About 9.8 lakh members paid for fitness services on the company’s platform in FY26. The fitness products business shipped more than 42.3 lakh products during the year.Fitness services bring in about 70% of its revenue, while products account for the remaining 30%, the company said. It sells workout clothes, shoes, fitness equipment, cycles and accessories through its app, website and other channels.Cult Elite centres offer gym workouts and trainer-led group classes, including yoga, dance, strength training and boxing. Cult Neo centres focus on gym workouts, with equipment designed in-house and certified trainers.Redseer expects India’s fitness services market to grow from Rs 25,600 crore in 2025 to between Rs 48,700 crore and Rs 53,100 crore by 2030.The company plans to list its shares on the BSE and the NSE stock exchanges. Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, JM Financial and Morgan Stanley are managing the issue.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Wall Street's main stock indexes were lower on Friday, as renewed selling in technology and chip stocks weighed on the broader market amid concerns over rising borrowing costs and debt-funded investments in artificial intelligence (AI).The S&P 500 fell 0.61%, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.3%, putting both indexes on track for weekly losses. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was nearly flat, up 0.01%, and headed for a weekly gain, Reuters reported.Technology stocks remained under pressure as investors reassessed the financing behind the AI infrastructure boom. CoreWeave shares fell 9% on Friday and were on track to lose nearly 23% for the week, amid growing scrutiny of the funding required for large-scale AI infrastructure investments."We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund, told Reuters.Concerns over inflation and the prospect of higher interest rates have also unsettled markets. Stronger-than-expected US consumer and wholesale inflation data this week prompted traders to increase bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes.Meanwhile, US Treasury yields eased on Friday as bond markets stabilised following a rush towards safe-haven assets in the previous session. The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note stood at 5.085%, according to Reuters.Among individual stocks, Micron Technology, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom and Intel declined, while gains in financial stocks helped limit broader market losses.Elsewhere, Brent crude futures rose 0.85% to $106.83 per barrel, supported by concerns over oil supplies amid heightened tensions in the Middle East and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz.You use AI every day. articles.title: Instant house-help race heats up as losses mount
articles.summary: Instant house-help race heats up: Urban Company Q2 loss Rs 182.5 crore; Snabbit Ebitda loss Rs 145 crore as both spend to scale InstaHelp demand.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Urban Company is losing more money, and its chief executive Abhiraj Singh Bhal said it is choosing to do so. The company is spending heavily to become the app households turn to when their regular help takes a day off. Rival Snabbit is pursuing the same customers, with steep losses of its own. “The losses are high because we are choosing to keep them high and we are choosing to invest from a position of strength,” Bhal told analysts on Friday.Urban Company’s losses more than tripled to Rs 182.5 crore in the September quarter from Rs 59.3 crore a year earlier. Total income rose 40% to Rs 578.5 crore.Snabbit reported an Ebitda loss of Rs 145 crore for the Sept quarter in figures shared by founder Aayush Agarwal. Snabbit completed 64.5 lakh jobs, with a net transaction value of Rs 73 crore. Ebitda is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. The last two spread asset costs over time. Net loss is the final figure after all income, expenses and taxes are accounted for.Snabbit’s FY26 accounts also showed a loss of Rs 167.8 crore against Rs 5.7 crore a year earlier. Total income was Rs 27 crore, more than half coming from other income, mainly interest on bank deposits, according to regulatory filings sourced via Tofler.Agarwal offered a similar defence of spending on customer adoption, training, technology and expansion. “We made those investments deliberately, and we’d make them again,” he said. He said Snabbit’s loss per job had fallen below Rs 200 in September from about Rs 1,500 at the beginning of FY26.At InstaHelp, orders grew 63% sequentially to 62.3 lakh. Adjusted Ebitda loss widened to Rs 174 crore from Rs 132 crore in the June quarter, although loss per order fell to Rs 279 from Rs 346. Net order value declined to Rs 114 from Rs 138 amid competition and introductory offers. Urban Company’s adjusted Ebitda also excludes items such as share-based employee costs.Higher prices could test how much demand lasts. Bhal said InstaHelp would need pricing of roughly Rs 200 an hour and an average order value of Rs 300 for bookings lasting about 90 minutes. That assumes worker payouts of about Rs 150 an hour.“Once pricing fully corrects, we will see a downward correction in the orders,” he said.Urban Company’s board has approved raising up to Rs 2,500 crore through routes that could include qualified institutional placements (QIPs), subject to shareholder approval. It held Rs 1,901 crore in cash and treasury investments at September-end.“The incremental capital allows us to be more aggressive,” Bhal said. The money would support growth and potential acquisitions, although he described an acquisition in InstaHelp as “highly unlikely”.The board also approved exploring residential air conditioners under Native, its water purifier and smart lock brand. Bhal said the first one or two years would focus on learning, largely through its app.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jim Cramer doubles down on his stock market stand
articles.summary: Confusing markets have a way of testing investors; Cramer thinks most will fail that test.
articles.body:
Markets posted broad losses on Oct. 14, with the S&P 500 falling just over 1%, the Nasdaq dropping 1.9% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average closing modestly lower. The declines came as investors weighed a hotter-than-expected inflation report, rising oil prices and growing uncertainty around Federal Reserve policy.

The session offered few clear signals. Strong quarterly results from two widely followed companies failed to support their shares, Treasury yields moved in ways that contradicted historical patterns, and geopolitical risk added another layer of pressure. Jim Cramer watched all of it and offered a direct response.

The CNBC host told investors to stay in the market. He argued that attempting to time an exit during a confusing stretch could prove far more costly than riding out the volatility.

The foundation of Cramer's argument was JPMorgan Chase research tracking S&P 500 returns over a 20-year period. An investor who put $10,000 into the index in 2005 and stayed fully invested through 2024 would have accumulated substantially more than one who missed the index's 10 best trading days across those two decades.

The gap was not small. The investor who sat out just those 10 sessions ended with less than half the wealth of the one who stayed in throughout. Those best days, Cramer noted, rarely announce themselves in advance.

Investors who sell during a downturn often do so to prevent further losses. The sharpest single-day gains, though, tend to arrive during the same stretches of peak volatility. That is when sitting out the market feels like the only reasonable move.

Cramer said investors who "throw things away and go home" face a harder problem than avoiding further declines. Buying back in after a sharp recovery means paying more than an investor who never left, and the timing of that recovery is rarely predictable.

The September consumer price index rose 0.6% from the prior month, above analyst estimates. The report sent Treasury yields higher initially as investors priced in a more aggressive Federal Reserve response to the hotter-than-expected reading.

Yields reversed later in the session even as oil prices continued to climb. The divergence was notable. Hotter inflation typically keeps yields elevated by sustaining expectations for higher interest rates, but that relationship broke down Oct. 14 as bonds recovered ground.

articles.title: Nasdaq sinks more than 2% as investors raise questions about AI debt
articles.summary: Tech stocks had a tumultuous week as concerns, including higher interest rates and mounting AI debt, continued to weigh on investor sentiment.
articles.body: Tech stocks had a tumultuous week as concerns, including higher interest rates and mounting AI debt, continued to weigh on investor sentiment. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.14% on Friday, bringing its weekly losses to roughly 4.5% — its worst week since June. The S&P 500 fell 1.09%, putting its weekly losses at almost 2%, also its worst week since June. The Nasdaq and S&P clinched record highs just 10 days ago. But since then, the market has stumbled as jitters spread about whether rising borrowing costs will put pressure on risky corners of the AI boom that are reliant on debt. At the center of concerns is a niche group called neoclouds, which rent computing power to companies in the AI boom. CoreWeave (CRWV), a neocloud that went public in 2025 and is backed by Nvidia, has emerged as a particular source of market anxiety. CoreWeave has tens of billions of dollars of debt on its balance sheet as it borrows money to fund its growth. Recently, its bond yields surged to levels that signal distress, or a higher risk of default. “It’s unclear that (CoreWeave is) going to get a sufficiently good return to pay down the debt that they borrowed,” Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, told CNN. “As people get concerned about the trajectory of the buildout, they are the subprime tranche of the AI trade, and that’s why they’re selling off first.” Luria said he thinks demand for AI is real and growing, but for companies like CoreWeave, that’s in tension with concerns about unsustainable financing and steep interest rates. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped in to assuage concerns on Thursday, telling Bloomberg that he’s optimistic about CoreWeave, an endorsement that helped the company’s stock rally on Thursday. But it was short-lived: The stock dropped almost 12% on Friday. CoreWeave shares lost one-quarter of their value this week. The stock is down more than 65% since a peak shortly after its IPO in March 2025. Meanwhile, oil prices jumped Friday and Brent crude touched $110 per barrel for the first time since May, exacerbating concerns about inflationary pressures that could push the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates further. Chipmaker jitters Adding to market anxiety this week: A sharp drop in semiconductor chipmakers, the so-called “picks and shovels” of the AI boom. A closely watched index of semiconductor chip stocks dropped 3.8% on Friday, falling for the eighth day in a row. The index slumped 11.4% on the week, its worst weekly performance since April 2025. Investors sent chip stocks soaring this year on expectations for a massive AI buildout and a shortage of chips that would allow the companies to reap enormous profits. But those stocks are losing their luster as Wall Street reckons with concerns about rising costs and the politicization of data centers that could hamper forecasts for the buildout. Meanwhile, semiconductor stocks haven’t recovered since Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT announced earlier this week that it made headway on advanced memory chips. The development is roiling investors who were betting US and South Korean chipmakers would have a dominant market share and pricing power, and are now debating whether cheaper, efficient chips from China could spoil that outlook. “The market sells first, asks questions later,” said Thomas Martin, portfolio manager at Globalt Investments. “That’s why you get the volatility.” The semis index is down more than 20% since a peak in June, although it’s still up more than 50% year-to-date. South Korea’s stock market had a tumultuous week. The benchmark Kospi index is heavily weighted in just two companies: chipmaker titans SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. The Kospi tumbled 14.5% this week, its worst weekly performance since 2008. The Kospi had soared this year, and in June was up as much as 116% year-to-date. But the Kospi has wiped out all of its gains across the past six months and is now up 35% year-to-date. Semiconductor chips, critical for AI, have become an increasingly important part of the stock market. The semis industry accounts for roughly one-fifth of the S&P 500’s market value. Further losses could spell trouble for the broader market. Wall Street’s fear gauge, the VIX, surged more than 20% on Friday and rose above 20 points — a level that signals elevated volatility in markets. All told, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are down roughly 2% and 5%, respectively, since their peaks earlier this month.

articles.title: New airfare rules: Govt won’t cap charges but ensure no sudden spike in ‘exceptional’ situations
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. However, it will keep a “strong lever” on airlines to ensure they don’t resort to very sharp surges in “exceptional and extra ordinary circumstances” that see demand rising for certain routes.The new policy will require airlines to determine charges based on their “cost of operations.” Airlines will submit a range of fares charges on different routes to the DGCA periodically. This will help ensure no one beyond the maximum given fares.The Centre had on Friday informed the Supreme Court that administrative approval has been granted to the rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, and they are likely to be published within two weeks.“We are on the verge of finalising the new rules. However, govt will not regulate airfares in a free market, especially given the severe cost stress under which airlines are operating. We will ensure in public interest ensure under no circumstances they charge more than the highest fare bucket submitted to the regulator,” said people in the know.Govt will have the power to act in “exceptional and extra ordinary” circumstances to regulate fares for a limited period of the exigency like natural calamity when there’s a sudden demand from people to fly in or out of some place. Most recently the same was seen post the Pahalgam attack last April when almost all tourists in Kashmir wanted to fly out of Srinagar at the earliest. “This action (to regulate fares in exceptional situations) will be proportionate to the severity of the situation and be in place for only as long as required,” said sources.The DGCA will decide the periodicity in which airlines will be required to submit the range of fares to it for each route. “Airlines will share the total amount to be charged along with break-up of the same in terms of various components like base fare, taxes, surcharge and airport/user development fees of origin and destination airports. They will also share their refund policy in terms of which all components will be refunded in case of cancellations,” said sources.Instead of taking a populist route on fares, the Union aviation ministry has kept the realities of Indian airlines in which most of them are struggling to survive. The rising jet fuel prices have broken their backs. The rupee’s weakening has added to the crisis as a majority of costs like lease rentals and maintenance contracts are dollar denominated. The global geopolitical situation, especially closure of Pakistan airspace for almost 17 months now, has made things even worse.“We are all aware of airlines’ financial health. There used to be one profitable airline which is also now in the red. As long as they are not unreasonable in times of crisis, we have no intention of interfering in airfares. If anything, we are going to give them more freedom and expect them to be good samaritans in exceptional circumstances,” added sources.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Is Anthropic worth $2 trillion? How about $1.5 trillion?
articles.summary: Anthropic's AI tools are revolutionary, but how much is the leading AI lab actually worth as a public company?
articles.body:
Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) work will contribute to massive changes in the US economy and workforce , but how much is the leading AI lab actually worth as a public company?

Reuters, citing several people familiar with the matter, reported that current and prospective investors in Anthropic's initial public offering who attended an investor day at Anthropic's San Francisco headquarters this week discussed a valuation of the Claude maker at about $1.5 trillion, down from earlier expectations of $2 trillion.

"What's $500 billion between friends in the AI trade?" Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley quipped (video above) before adding, "It does get to the point of you're trying to justify these huge valuations: Do your numbers justify it?"

Anthropic's third quarter revenue reportedly rose 45% from the second quarter to $16.8 billion, and the company stayed profitable on an adjusted basis. Reuters, which got its hands on Anthropic's IPO prospectus , previously reported that revenue more than doubled in the second quarter, to $11.6 billion from $4.7 billion.

"While those numbers assuaged some concerns about the massive costs of developing AI systems," Reuters reported, "some investors were disappointed by the slowing sequential growth rate in the latest quarter."

Yahoo Finance co-host Julie Hyman called the lower price "a reading-the-room moment," with AI stocks selling off this week . "All of this would seem to indicate that there's at least enough concern out there that you're not going to go out and try and overprice."

Hyman also noted that one quarter may not settle it: "We don't know if it's going to reaccelerate in the fourth quarter."

Conley wants a different yardstick than annual recurring revenue (ARR), the run-rate figure AI companies like to cite.

"ARR, that's not a real number," he said. "Give me some GAAP numbers."

articles.title: Charles Schwab CEO: AI agents trading on your behalf need 'rules of the road'
articles.summary: The rise of AI-driven trading on investing platforms is not lost on Charles Schwab CEO Rick Wurster.
articles.body:
The rise of AI-driven trading on platforms such as Robinhood ( HOOD ) and Coinbase ( COIN ) is not lost on Charles Schwab ( SCHW ) CEO Rick Wurster. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)

He's down with it — as long as there are proper guidelines.

"I think if you have an AI agent that is trading on your behalf, you have given it a lot of thought. I think an AI agent should only trade on your behalf if you give them the rules of the road," Wurster said on Yahoo Finance.

"You work with them to build a process, just like you come on our site today and research a stock, put in a limit order. That's how I think you're going to need to work with an agent," he added. "The idea that you would just say to an agent, 'Hey, go buy me stocks and trade for me,' I think that is risky. But to be able to say, 'Hey, here's how I want to buy stocks. Here's my methodology. Here's my process, and I'm going to oversee this,' I think that makes sense. But just handing the keys over, I think that, to me, that's a leap too far. It is risky."

The brokerage giant will soon debut Charley, the company's new AI-powered conversational assistant. It will not be an agentic trading bot .

Out of the gate, Charley will be able to take action on a client's behalf for some administrative tasks, such as changing an address or naming a trusted contact. Over time, the company envisions it becoming a "front door" to the Charles Schwab platform.

Charles Schwab had a generally solid third quarter without AI agents trading on behalf of humans, though Wall Street saw a few yellow flags.

Adjusted earnings rose 29% year over year to $1.69 a share, topping Wall Street expectations. Revenue climbed 17% to a record $7.17 billion, just shy of analyst estimates.

The company benefited from a surge in trading activity, fresh client assets, and higher interest income.

Charles Schwab attracted a record $190.4 billion in core net new assets, up 38% from a year ago, as daily average trading volume jumped 44% to 10.7 million trades. Net interest revenue increased 14% to $3.48 billion.

The company said full-year revenue and expense growth would be toward the low ends of its prior ranges of +17.5–18.5% and +9.5–10.5%, respectively.

"An expense driven EPS beat was overshadowed by the net interest income miss and softer fiscal year guidance. In our view, the main takeaway is that organic growth looks strong, with record NNA of $190 billion, and client lending demand remains healthy, but slower client cash growth is increasing reliance on higher-cost wholesale funding and pressuring the near-term NIM outlook," Evercore ISI analyst Glenn Schorr said.

articles.title: Meta employees say Lula’s accounts restricted in Brazil election: Report
articles.summary: The messages, reported by a Brazilian daily, say the platform recommended Bolsonaro’s profile and his WhatsApp channel.
articles.body:
Employees at Meta have acknowledged in internal communications that the Instagram accounts of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were negatively affected by restrictions during the country’s election, media reports say.

The messages, reported on Friday by Brazilian daily Folha de S Paulo, also acknowledged the platform recommended the profile of Lula challenger Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, as well as his WhatsApp channel. Folha, the Sao Paulo-based paper, cited messages it had reviewed.

Meta told the Reuters news agency that the technical issues cited in the report were already public and the conversations it referenced related solely to the severity of the issues, not political interference.

“Any suggestion that Meta favors one side is false,” it added in a statement.

Lula, the left-wing incumbent, will face right-wing challenger Bolsonaro in a presidential runoff on October 25, following a stronger-than-expected performance by the senator in the first-round vote earlier this month.

Friday’s report came on the heels of a Brazilian court ruling on Thursday that ordered Meta to immediately adopt measures to provide equal treatment of the two candidates ahead of the runoff.

The ruling by a judge in Brazil’s top electoral court was made shortly after Lula filed a complaint that accused the tech giant – which owns Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp – of using biased algorithms and AI restrictions to favour opposition candidate Bolsonaro ahead of the election.

Justice Marco Aurelio Bellizze ruled that Meta cannot reduce the distribution of political content, restrict searches or remove posts in a way that creates an imbalance between Lula and Bolsonaro. His ruling also orders the company to ensure its artificial intelligence tool applies identical criteria to both candidacies.

Bellizze said in his ruling that Meta must pay a fine of 500,000 reais ($98,700) per day if it fails to comply.

According to Lula’s party, some of his posts appeared without a share button and had reduced reach. Options for reactions, sharing, audio or accelerated speed were also missing.
